reviewScope: First bounded inspection of exactly the four original saved images named by views[0/1].screenshot and definitionScreenshot. Observe nonblank content, heading and crumb, discernible legibility, framing, paragraph separation, rendered equation forms and emphasis, and mobile fit. No browser, rendering, new screenshots, crops or reopens.

observations: Nonblank black serif prose sits in a centered, constrained column on white, with generous side margins. The heading is visibly Boyle's law explained by the kinetic theory.
The smaller muted crumb is separate from the heading and wraps cleanly. Part One, Chapter 2 Fundamentals of thermodynamics, and printed page 27 are discernible.

The initial question, model assumptions, wall-collision explanation, equilibrium discussion, and real-gas ending remain visually separated. Thin dividers distinguish conceptual transitions without covering text.

Rendered n and p inverse-volume expressions show proportionality and stacked reciprocal forms rather than raw TeX; pV appears inline in the later paragraph. The bold ideal-gas statement stands out without colliding with its following text.
The final deviation paragraph and bottom whitespace are visible. No apparent overlapping paragraphs, horizontal clipping, missing body region, or obstructed ending is seen at supplied-preview scale.
This exact named image is an opening viewport, not a polarization figure. It contains the title and crumb, opening question, model paragraphs and start of the collision argument.

The viewport preview permits a closer check of normal-size sentence text: dark text is crisp enough to read, spacing distinguishes paragraphs, and the number-density discussion fits inside the column.
The reciprocal number-density expression is visible near the bottom. Content beyond the viewport is not claimed to be covered by this image alone.
The title wraps to two lines and the smaller crumb to several short lines, with visible separation from the first paragraph. Neither is visibly cut off on the sides.
Prose is presented as a narrow single column with consistent left/right padding. Paragraphs wrap naturally and remain distinguishable through the full-page sequence.
The reciprocal n and p expressions and inline pV are recognizable, contained in the text column, and do not visibly overwrite neighboring lines.
The bold ideal-gas emphasis wraps across lines cleanly. The final real-gas deviation paragraph remains visible with bottom whitespace.
No apparent horizontal overflow, squeezed heading, overlapping paragraph region, or blank middle section is visible in the supplied long preview.

This saved image is a scrolled excerpt spanning the end of the model assumptions and the wall-collision/number-density discussion. It does not show the heading or breadcrumb; those were inspected in the whole image.

Its first line meets the top scroll boundary, which is a viewport boundary rather than evidence of horizontal layout failure. Complete lines below it remain readable and framed inside the mobile margins.
The separation before the wall-collision paragraph is clear. The long conditions sentence wraps without an apparent collision or cropped word on either side.
The inline density symbol n is visible near the end. The two reciprocal equations and later bold statement are outside this excerpt and are not claimed as close-view checks here.

conclusion: PASS for these four bound saved-pixel previews. Both views show nonblank, coherently framed English lesson content, readable paragraph regions, clean heading/crumb treatment where visible, and recognizable equation/emphasis rendering. No required visual correction is identified within this bounded scope.
